note: Limits of the investment plan. A limit set to null is not checked. Active risk (5-day 97.5% expected shortfall against the S&P 500) is calculated by the allocation model (models/igfinal/config.py).
buy_criteria: Replica of the S&P 500: its 50 largest companies at index weights, without NVIDIA (very high volatility) and, since 19 November, without Oracle (replaced by Citigroup on Andrea's recommendation).
Berkshire Hathaway is held at 10% of the fund as a defensive position (portfolio manager, 19 November); the replica fills the other 90%.
From 16 to 19 November a sleeve of 30% of the fund (AMD, ASML, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, PLTR, BABA, 3.75% each) was held for the Anthropic IPO.

On 20 November: with a lead over the benchmark of at least 0.5 points the fund moves to the sector-balanced replica; otherwise it keeps the 50 largest. At the 19 November close the fund was 3.17 points behind, so it keeps the 50 largest.
Every order is approved by the portfolio manager and recorded in the trade log with its reason.
sell_criteria: The IPO sleeve was sold in full on 19 November after the New York open, as fixed in advance (even if the IPO had been delayed).
From 27 November the fund is brought back to its target weights every Friday morning, always fully invested.
An order smaller than $10,000 (0.1% of the fund) is not placed: it costs a commission and changes almost nothing.
A breached limit is fixed before any other trade: a stock above 15% is trimmed back to its target; if active expected shortfall is above its limit, the positions that contribute most to it are sold.
Market orders only; no short selling.
